clue.text: Children's toy! For little squirts, anyway

definitions.text: Children's toy! For little squirts, anyway

parts.words: Children's toy! For little squirts, anyway
parts.note: a toy for children, who are 'little squirts'; it also literally squirts, so the phrase works both ways

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain plaything suits small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little squirts' is slang for small children, and the toy in question shoots little squirts of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaything that shoots jets of liquid is a classic children's garden toy.

clue.text: Argue about crafty trick to get the king in

indicators.note: with 'in' after it, says one piece takes another inside it
completes 'to get ... in', the instruction to place the king within the trick

parts.note: a wangle is a crafty piece of manipulation
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone bickers over a sly scheme to smuggle a monarch inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get ... in' puts R inside WANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrangle is to dispute noisily, a synonym of quarrel.

clue.text: Rows may lead to them, by the sound of it!

indicators.note: says the word suggested must be heard, not seen, to give the entry

parts.note: rows (quarrels) may end in weeping, drops from the eyes

explanation.surface: An observation that arguments can end in weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' reads as quarrels (rhyming with cows), but the definition is rows (rhyming with toes), layers one above another.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows of seats rising one above another, as in a stadium, are ranked levels.

clue.text: Left — right!

parts.note: 'Left' as in what remains behind, followed by an approving 'right!' confirming that sense

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant barking marching orders.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is soldiers marching left, right; the real sense is 'left' as the amount remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over after a process is the remainder or remnant.

clue.text: Wants to be sure he gets it, he does

definitions.text: Wants to be sure he gets it, he does

parts.words: Wants to be sure he gets it, he does
parts.note: describes someone demanding firmly that he receives something, refusing to be put off

explanation.surface: Someone determined to make certain he receives his due.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who demands something firmly and will not yield is said to be adamant about it.

clue.text: Journeyman representative? EC 4 P

definitions.meaning: taken literally, a man who journeys, one on the road
a commercial representative selling on the road for a firm

explanation.surface: A job title followed by a London postal code, like a business card.
explanation.walkthrough: EC4P was the Fleet Street postcode of the Telegraph, so the sales rep is from the paper's own office; it adds colour but no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer journeys, and a sales rep who visits customers is called a commercial one too.

clue.text: Ancestors occupation for a time

parts.note: a line of work is a trade or occupation
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Forebears who followed one trade for an era.
explanation.definitionFit: One's line of descent, the family's forebears, is one's ancestry.

clue.text: Said to go to Heaven

parts.note: words spoken aloud in worship are believed to rise up to God

explanation.surface: A pious claim about where something ends up.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotional petitions addressed to God are spoken in the hope they reach Him.

clue.text: Deck hands come from here

parts.note: a 'deck' is a set of playing cards, and 'hands' are what players are dealt from it

explanation.surface: Asking where sailors are recruited.
explanation.walkthrough: Deck hands look like sailors; it is card hands dealt from a deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A full deck of fifty-two playing cards is what card hands are dealt from.

clue.text: But such glass is not dirty

definitions.text: But such glass is not dirty

parts.words: But such glass is not dirty
parts.note: glass described with a word for soiled, yet it is coloured on purpose, as in church windows

explanation.surface: A paradox about glass that sounds grubby but is clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured church window glass is called by a word that otherwise means soiled or marked.

clue.text: Ties them on top of such evening attire

definitions.text: Ties them on top of such evening attire

parts.words: Ties them on top of such evening attire
parts.note: bow ties are worn over the formal garments men put on with a dinner jacket

explanation.surface: Dressing instructions for a formal evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal shirts with stiff fronts are worn under black or white tie for evening.

clue.text: Holding charges made by barmen?

parts.note: 'charges' as things in one's keeping, held by structures made of bars

explanation.surface: Asking about the bar bill a publican keeps running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barmen' and 'charges' suggest a pub tab; here barmen are makers of bars, and charges are animals held captive.
explanation.definitionFit: Barred enclosures hold animals or birds captive.

clue.text: Is hopelessly reckless about speed &velocity!

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters of speed are rearranged

parts.note: a rate is a speed or velocity

explanation.surface: Someone driving wildly fast with no regard for safety.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate action is wild and reckless because there seems no hope left.

clue.text: Manage to give medical aid

definitions.meaning: to run or work something, such as a machine
what a surgeon does in theatre

explanation.definitionFit: To work a machine and to perform surgery share one verb meaning to run or to cut.

clue.text: Bill has a string, one on a musical instrument

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a cord is a string
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bill with string attached, as if paying for an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The squeezebox, a bellows-driven keyboard instrument, is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Iron necessary for joiner who does so

definitions.text: Iron necessary for joiner who does so

parts.words: Iron necessary for joiner who does so
parts.note: a soldering iron is the tool of someone joining metal with molten alloy

explanation.surface: A carpenter needing an iron, as if for pressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter; here it is anyone joining metals with a hot iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who joins metal pieces with molten alloy uses a heated iron for the job.

clue.text: We can pick things from them

definitions.text: We can pick things from them

parts.words: We can pick things from them
parts.note: a range of options from which a selection is made

explanation.surface: A remark about orchards or shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: Options or selections are what one picks from.

clue.text: Given the chance to have bad deer chop

parts.note: food gone bad has gone off

indicators.note: to chop is to cut up, so the letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone offered rotten venison cutlets.
explanation.definitionFit: If something has been presented to you for acceptance, you have been given the chance of it.

clue.text: Genuine synonym!

parts.note: the clue simply asks for another word meaning genuine, as in heartfelt

explanation.surface: A thesaurus entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt and honest feeling is genuine.

clue.text: Rack&pinion put back to front to do this!

definitions.text: Rack&pinion put back to front to do this!

parts.words: Rack&pinion put back to front to do this!
parts.note: the rack, a torture device, pulls the limbs out, and pinioning arms back does likewise

explanation.surface: An engineer reversing a rack-and-pinion gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Rack and pinion sounds like gearing; the rack here is the torture frame that pulls a body longer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack elongates the body, pulling limbs to extend them.

clue.text: Did it in order to get letters

definitions.text: Did it in order to get letters

parts.words: Did it in order to get letters
parts.note: putting letters in their correct order to form words

explanation.surface: Someone acting so as to receive post.
explanation.definitionFit: Naming or writing a word's letters in correct sequence is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Three banks pulled out of this shipbuilding enterprise

definitions.text: Three banks pulled out of this shipbuilding enterprise

parts.words: Three banks pulled out of this shipbuilding enterprise
parts.note: an ancient galley with three banks of oars pulled by rowers

explanation.surface: Financial news: three lenders withdraw from a shipyard venture.
explanation.walkthrough: The banks look like lenders; they are tiers of oars, pulled by rowers.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek warship with three tiers of oars.

clue.text: Used to be a character important to the map-reader

definitions.text: Used to be a character important to the map-reader

parts.words: Used to be a character important to the map-reader
parts.note: a testimonial of character, and the grid coordinates a map-reader uses

explanation.surface: A navigator who once had a colourful personality.
explanation.definitionFit: A testimonial about character and a grid location on a map share this word.

clue.text: Pipe stem with spikes on it

definitions.meaning: a tobacco pipe made of heath root wood
a thorny, prickly shoot of a rose or bramble

explanation.definitionFit: Both a tobacco pipe of heath wood and a thorny shoot share this name.

clue.text: Short work for a lawyer

definitions.meaning: a case given to a barrister

explanation.definitionFit: Concise in length, and also a barrister's instructions for a case.

clue.text: Hussar dines on some fish

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cavalry soldier eats a meal of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily fish of the herring family, often tinned.

clue.text: Perhaps, in a way, doesn't move

definitions.text: Perhaps, in a way, doesn't move

parts.words: Perhaps, in a way, doesn't move
parts.note: hanging about in a street or way without moving on, which is only loosely 'not moving'

explanation.surface: A hedged remark about something staying put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' is a road: someone hanging about in the road does not move on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lingers idly in a public place is hanging about, not moving on.

clue.text: Feed-one laid out for a writer

indicators.note: laid out suggests spread and rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A novelist laying out a meal for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Robinson Crusoe was an English novelist and journalist.
